title: Finite projective-line splitting and diagonal integrals over arbitrary bases
statement:
Let $N\geq1$ be an integer, let $A$ be a finite commutative ring with $NA=0$, and let $S$ be any scheme [def-pc-scheme] on which $N$ is invertible. Work on small ordinary etale sites with the unbounded module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], inverse image [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], unbounded derived direct image [def-kun-unbounded-exchange], and derived tensor [def-kun-derived-tensor]. For every scheme $T$ over $S$, put $P_T=\mathbf P(\{0,1\};T)=\mathbf P^1_T$ and $r_T:P_T\to T$ [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change]. Let $A_T$ denote the constant coefficient sheaf. Put $A_T(1)=\mu_{N,T}\otimes_{(\mathbf Z/N)_T}A_T$, with roots of unity, scalar action and inverse-image identifications as in [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]. Let $h_T:A_T\to Rr_{T,*}A_{P_T}(1)[2]$ be the adjoint of the scalar-extended Kummer first Chern class of the hyperplane line bundle $\mathcal O_{P_T}(1)$, obtained by gluing the affine-base constructions [def-pc-projective-space-twist], and the Kummer sequence [lem-amb-kummer-any-base]. Then the map
$$b_T:A_T(1)[2]\oplus A_T\longrightarrow Rr_{T,*}A_{P_T}(1)[2]$$
whose first component is the shifted twisted inverse-image/direct-image unit and whose second component is $h_T$ is an isomorphism. Write $t_T=\operatorname{pr}_2b_T^{-1}$. For every morphism $v:T'\to T$, the canonical proper exchange [def-kun-unbounded-exchange] and the twist pullback identification carry $b_T$ and $t_T$ to $b_{T'}$ and $t_{T'}$.

Put $P=P_S$, $W=P\times_SP$, and let $p_1,p_2:W\to P$ be the two projections [def-pc-fibre-product]. The diagonal $\Delta:P\hookrightarrow W$ is an effective Cartier divisor [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal]. Let $\delta_A=c_{\Delta,A}:R\Delta_*A_P\to A_W(1)[2]$ be its supported Kummer morphism, with the sign convention $c_{\Delta,A}u_\Delta=c_1(\mathcal O_W(\Delta))$ [lem-asd-ordinary-supported-kummer]. For $i=1,2$, identify $p_i$ with $r_P:\mathbf P^1_P\to P$, and let $\alpha_i:A_P\xrightarrow{\sim}Rp_{i*}R\Delta_*A_P$ be the canonical derived-composition identification for $p_i\Delta=1_P$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition]. Then
$$t_P\circ Rp_{i*}(\delta_A)\circ\alpha_i=1_{A_P}\qquad(i=1,2).$$
The base $S$ is not assumed Noetherian or of finite type over a field.

source.place: Levelwise check, finite diagonal integrals; agent arbitrary-base finite-coefficient interface (proof details retained in report.md)

proof.text: Put $U=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[1/N]$, $Q=\mathbf P^1_U$ and $r_U:Q\to U$. Every scheme on which $N$ is invertible has its canonical map to $U$: on affine opens the map sends $a/N^k$ to $a(N^{-1})^k$, and these maps agree on overlaps. The ring $\mathbf Z[1/N]$ is Noetherian: for an ideal $J$, choose a generator $d$ of $J\cap\mathbf Z$; since $a/N^k\in J$ implies $a\in J\cap\mathbf Z$, one has $J=(d)$. Any ascending chain stabilizes because its union has one generator, already in some member. Thus [lem-asd-ordinary-finite-p1-adjunction] applies to $U$, $N$ and the given finite ring $A$. Its displayed $b_{r_U}$ has exactly the two components specified here, so $b_U$ is an isomorphism and $t_U=\operatorname{pr}_2 b_U^{-1}$.

source.place: Levelwise check, finite diagonal integrals; universal Noetherian base

proof.text: Over an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}R$ of any base $T$, [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-standard-charts] gives the two charts $\operatorname{Spec}R[t]$, $\operatorname{Spec}R[s]$, with $s=t^{-1}$ on the overlap. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], their product charts have polynomial coordinate rings in two variables. The equation $x_0y_1-x_1y_0=0$ restricts to a difference of the two coordinates on equal charts and to $1-tu$ up to a unit on mixed charts. Its zero subscheme is the diagonal: on equal charts it identifies the coordinates; on mixed charts the relation $tu=1$ identifies the two overlap coordinates. A monic difference is a non-zero-divisor by its leading coefficient. If $(1-tu)\sum a_k(u)t^k=0$, comparison of the constant coefficient and then successive coefficients gives $a_0=a_1=\cdots=0$. Thus the diagonal is effective Cartier by [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal]. The hyperplane $H=(x_1=0)$ has equation $t$ on the $x_0$ chart and is empty on the $x_1$ chart. Its ideal dual [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle] has bases with transition $e_0=t^{-1}e_1$, precisely $\mathcal O(1)$ in the chart statement. All these equations and transitions remain the same over every new base ring, so diagonal and hyperplane pullbacks are still effective Cartier and $\mathcal O(H)$ pulls back to $\mathcal O(1)$.

source.place: Standard-chart proof of the effective Cartier diagonal and hyperplane; arbitrary base change

proof.text:
For $v:T'\to T$ over $U$, let $v_P:P_{T'}\to P_T$ be the induced map. The morphism $r_T$ is proper by [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-proper]. Since $NA=0$, [lem-kun-proper-base-change-torsion-ring] gives the canonical exchange isomorphism $B_v:v^{-1}Rr_{T,*}A_{P_T}(1)[2]\xrightarrow{\sim}Rr_{T',*}A_{P_{T'}}(1)[2]$. Use [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback] to identify coefficients and let $\sigma_v:v^{-1}(A_T(1)[2]\oplus A_T)\xrightarrow{\sim}A_{T'}(1)[2]\oplus A_{T'}$. Then
$$B_v\,v^{-1}b_T=b_{T'}\sigma_v.$$
For the first component this is the unit identity for the exchange mate [def-kun-unbounded-exchange], obtained by inserting its unit-counit formula and cancelling the adjacent counit-unit pair. For the second component, express $c_1(\mathcal O(1))$ as $c_{H,A}u_H$. By Step 2 the pulled-back hyperplane is effective Cartier with line bundle $\mathcal O(1)$, so [lem-asd-ordinary-supported-kummer] identifies the pulled-back supported morphism with $c_{H',A}$. The divisor unit satisfies the same mate identity, so the composite pulls back to $c_{H',A}u_{H'}$. Taking adjoints gives precisely $h_{T'}$. The two component equations prove the displayed equality without assuming that $b_T$ is already invertible.

source.place: Levelwise check, base-change normalization of the two defining components

proof.text:
Apply Step 3 to the canonical $a:T\to U$. The equality $b_T=B_a\,a^{-1}b_U\,\sigma_a^{-1}$ shows that $b_T$ is an isomorphism, since all three factors are isomorphisms by Steps 1 and 3. Define $t_T=\operatorname{pr}_2 b_T^{-1}$. Invert the equality of Step 3 and use $\operatorname{pr}_2\sigma_v=v^{-1}\operatorname{pr}_2$ to get
$$t_{T'}B_v=v^{-1}t_T.$$
This proves both the arbitrary-base splitting and the asserted trace compatibility for every $v$.

source.place: Levelwise check, arbitrary-base splitting and trace by inverting the component square

proof.text:
Apply [lem-amb-p1-diagonal-integrals] with Noetherian base $U$, the same $N$ and the same finite ring $A$. For $W_U=Q\times_UQ$ it gives
$$t_{p_{i,U}}R(p_{i,U})_*(\delta_{A,U})\alpha_{i,U}=1_{A_Q}\quad(i=1,2).$$
The trace used there is defined in [def-amb-p1-trace] as $\operatorname{pr}_2 b^{-1}$ for the splitting with components the twisted unit and the Kummer hyperplane class. Hence its trace is exactly the $t_Q$ already constructed in Step 4 for either projection $p_{i,U}$. The supported class has the same sign normalization $c_{\Delta,A}u_\Delta=c_1(\mathcal O(\Delta))$, and $\alpha_{i,U}$ is the canonical composition identification, as required. No trace or integral theorem has been applied to a non-Noetherian base in this step.

source.place: Levelwise check, the finite diagonal identities on the universal Noetherian base

proof.text:
For a scheme $T\to U$, write $w:P_T\to Q$ and $z:W_T\to W_U$ for the base-change maps, and fix $i$. Let $B_E:w^{-1}R(p_{i,U})_*E\xrightarrow{\sim}R(p_{i,T})_*z^{-1}E$ be proper exchange, available by [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-proper] and [lem-kun-proper-base-change-torsion-ring]. Step 2 makes the pulled-back diagonal effective Cartier, so [lem-asd-ordinary-supported-kummer] identifies $z^{-1}\delta_{A,U}$ with $\delta_{A,T}$ under the closed-immersion exchange $D:z^{-1}R\Delta_{U,*}A_Q\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Delta_{T,*}A_{P_T}$. Put $C=R(p_{i,T})_*D\circ B_{R\Delta_{U,*}A_Q}$. Naturality of $B$ gives
$$B_{A_{W_U}(1)[2]}\,w^{-1}(R(p_{i,U})_*\delta_{A,U})=R(p_{i,T})_*\delta_{A,T}\,C.$$
Also $C\,w^{-1}\alpha_{i,U}=\alpha_{i,T}$. To check this last equality, use [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] to identify the two successive direct images with the direct image of $p_i\Delta=1$. Clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] identifies the composite exchange $C$ with the exchange for that composite, and clause (4) identifies the exchange for the identity with the identity. Thus the equation is a formal consequence of the canonical mate formulas, rather than an extra base-change assertion attributed to the composition node.

source.place: Levelwise check, explicit exchange equations for the supported class and composition identification

proof.text:
Combining the two equations of Step 6 with the trace equation of Step 4 gives
$$t_{P_T}R(p_{i,T})_*\delta_{A,T}\,\alpha_{i,T}=w^{-1}\bigl(t_Q R(p_{i,U})_*\delta_{A,U}\,\alpha_{i,U}\bigr)=w^{-1}1_{A_Q}=1_{A_{P_T}}.$$
The middle equality is Step 5, and inverse image preserves identities. This applies separately to $i=1,2$; take $T=S$ to obtain both integrals in the statement. All changes of base in Steps 3, 4 and 6 were arbitrary.

source.place: Levelwise check, pullback of the finite diagonal identity
